answer: When the snow melts the algae bloom red across the drifts, and the biologist samples each bloom and files the survey for the melt season. A beacon bloom claimed as sampled fails the survey: the sample must have been taken from the snow at the hollow of the melt, and a bloom never sampled has no cells to count. Forging a season of blooms means bribing the biologist, faking forty samples and paying 9,800, while the basalt survey is checked against the photographs, so a bloom whose sample was never taken fades with the snow.
